tests: R1: REPORTERS carries every reporter entry of the pinned reporters-db, with its editions, dates and variations
R1: VARIANTS maps every variant and standard abbreviation to each {reporter, edition}, never to one chosen
R2: COURTS carries every court of the pinned courts-db with its fields, and its name patterns translated
R3: SOURCES names each package's version, licence, files with their SHA-256, counts and whole licence text
R4: the build reads the pinned files and writes the one data module, every pattern compiling in JavaScript
R4: a file not at its pinned version is refused, and nothing is written
R4: Python templates and constructs are expanded and translated to equivalent JavaScript
R5: every example each package gives for a court or reporter matches its translated patterns; none untranslated
R5: a pattern whose translation fails its example is listed with its key and why, and never shipped
R6: verifyFresh answers true only for a byte-identical committed file, false for a changed one, null without the packages
R7: reporterFor answers VARIANTS' entries as written, then after folding white space and periods, else null
R7: courtsNamed answers every court one of whose patterns matches the whole text, in COURTS order, else []
R8: pure data, the same pinned versions give the same file, and no network, store or clock is used at run time
R9: kept apart from profiles: the data covers every court the package lists, and no answer depends on a place setting
R10: a recognised reporter or court is a spelling recognised, never a citation asserted real, resolved or verified
R11: evaluating the module builds none of the data; it is parsed once, on the first read of any export
R11: each export's first and later reads equal the committed data, read by the same names and shapes
R11 (R6): verifyFresh covers the data in its new form: one JSON text that parses to the build's data
